messages:
anya: Heads-up — noticed a sharp p99 jump on the `/v1/endpoint/generate-composite` tile right after we shifted route weights to the new shard. dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/d/abc123/generate-composite

mike: Is that the composite endpoint that rolls up per-model shards?

anya: yeah, it merges 4 underlying model routes (small/med/large + quantized). p50/p95 look fine, p99 up ~2.6x for the past ~20m.

rachit: Can you paste the dashboard query? suspecting merge artifact — mixing histograms with different bucket boundaries can inflate tail.

anya: query snippet from the tile: ```metric: request_latency_seconds histogram_aggregator: sum_by(endpoint) rollup: histogram buckets: auto```

rachit: there's the smell — we bucket before rollup. Different model shards emit different bucket edges (legacy client vs new runtime), so when we union them the rollup tdigest-like estimate is wrong. We should either normalize buckets at ingestion or switch that rollup to tdigest/proper quantile merge.

mike: Are we using histogram rollups for billing/quota? that would be problematic.

anya: billing uses token counters, but quota gating in console uses p95 from the same telemetry pipeline for some routes. not billing-critical now but affects alerting and routed fallback behavior.

rachit: short-term: add a tag to the composite rollup to split by `model_variant` so the dashboard shows subroute percentiles rather than a blind merged p99. long-term: change ingestion to emit consistent bucket boundaries or use tdigest for quantiles.

sarah: Adding split will help UX, but we also need to update rollout gating. Right now the canary policy compares endpoint p99 to baseline; merged p99 could trigger false failovers.

dashboard-bot: Canary deployment "route-weight/shard-2026-03-19" changed weights at 2026-03-19T14:02:11Z. Affected routes: generate-composite-{a,b,c,d}.

mike: Good catch. Can we have a short patch: show a small warning on the endpoint tile when the underlying route set has different histogram schemas? UX: yellow pill with "mixed histogram schemas — subroute breakdown recommended".

anya: I'll prototype the warning. Rachit — can you add a split-by tag and a small helper in telemetry to detect bucket-schema mismatch?

rachit: Yep. I can add a detector that compares bucket signatures for a given metric key. When mismatch detected, emit `histogram_schema_mismatch=true` and surface that in the console metadata. Plan: 1) detect mismatch 2) surface warning 3) auto-switch dashboard to subroute breakdown. Will open PR.

sarah: Also flag to SRE: if we temporarily disable p99 gating for that endpoint during the rollout window to avoid noisy rollbacks?

mike: Let's avoid disabling hard gates. Instead change the gating to evaluate the majority-of-shards p99 or use per-shard trending until we fix rollup. Safer.

anya: Action items summary: - Rachit add mismatch detector + split-by tag (PR) - Mike update gating logic to prefer per-shard compare - Me (anya) add console warning + small UX to expand subroute percentiles - Ops: monitor alerts for the next 24h and comment on the dashboard tile.

rachit: I'll target a tiny telemetry change today: sniff bucket fingerprints and emit the boolean tag. PR will include tests with mixed bucket families.

mike: After that, let's plan a migration: either standardize ingestion buckets (rollout at agent/runtime level) or migrate histogram rollups to tdigest-based quantile rollups with metadata for deterministic merges. Pros/cons doc needed.

anya: Agree — can we sync tomorrow 10am? I'll sketch the UX implications and example screenshots.

sarah: 10am works. Also add a quick note in the incident channel in case paging thresholds hit while we iterate.

anya: done — I'll create follow-up thread with PR links and UX mock. Thanks all :thumbsup:
